messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: [Name]

Sex: Male

Age: 76 years

Medical Record No.: [Number]

Hospital Admission Date: [Date]

Discharge Date: [Date]

Hospital Course:

A 76-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with an incidental 4 cm left renal mass, which was treated with a left partial nephrectomy. Upon pathological examination, it was discovered that the patient was suffering from WHO/ISUP grade 1, TNM stage pT1 clear cell RCC, with the resection margin positive for the tumor.

The patient underwent a right radical orchiectomy when he was found to have a metastatic tumor in the right testis. The metastatic tumor was two centimeters in size, and it was confined to the testicular parenchyma.

Fourteen months after the orchiectomy, he underwent a completion left radical nephrectomy due to the recurrence of the tumor.

Ongoing imaging surveillance discovered several soft tissue masses in the left posterior chest wall, as well as masses in the pancreas. A two-centimeter enhancing mass was found in the upper pole of the right kidney 87 months following the orchiectomy.

The patient has been offered systemic therapy of VEGF inhibitor and discharged with continued medical supervision. He is alive with disease, 93 months post-orchiectomy.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Status:

The patient is discharged with continued medical supervision.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The admission was for the incidental left renal mass, which pathology confirmed as clear cell renal cell carcinoma, the primary malignancy. The testicular, pancreatic and chest wall deposits are secondary sites of that same cancer, so they are not the principal diagnosis. Chapter C (neoplasms) category C64 covers malignant neoplasm of the kidney, excluding the renal pelvis.

CODE: C64
